subject: carbimazole
group: PTU dose in first trimester | mg
correct: In pregnancy PTU is given at the lowest effective dose to keep FT4 in the upper half of the reference range, specialist-led (SPC; RCOG GTG76 2025). 200–400 mg/day is the general adult starting dose, not a pregnancy dose.

fixes.old: • T1 (<14 wks): PTU 200–400mg/day — carbimazole embryopathy risk in organogenesis
fixes.new: • T1 (<14 wks): PTU at the lowest effective dose, specialist-led (switch from carbimazole as early as possible, before 10 weeks) — carbimazole embryopathy risk in organogenesis

note: The pregnancy bullet gives the non-pregnant adult starting range (200–400 mg/day) as the first-trimester dose. Over-treatment in pregnancy causes fetal hypothyroidism and goitre, and the SPC and RCOG say to use the lowest effective dose. The fix also adds RCOG's switch-before-10-weeks point. The 'around 20 weeks' switch back to carbimazole matches RCOG GTG76 2025 (as quoted by Wiles et al. 2025), so it is left unchanged.

subject: anaemia in pregnancy
correct: BSH 2020: Hb <110 g/L (T1) or <105 g/L (T2/T3) → oral iron and recheck in 2–3 weeks, under midwife/primary care. Refer to secondary care if Hb <70 g/L, significant symptoms, advanced gestation (>34 weeks) or no response.

fixes.old: • Pregnancy: Hb <110 g/L (1st trimester), <105 (later) → Same-day maternity; bleeding or compromise → 999
fixes.new: • Pregnancy: Hb <110 g/L (1st trimester), <105 (later) → start oral iron and inform the midwife; Hb <70 g/L, significant symptoms, rapid fall or late gestation (>34 weeks) → Same-day maternity; bleeding or compromise → 999

note: Read literally, the one-page sends every pregnant woman whose Hb is below the anaemia threshold for same-day maternity assessment. That conflicts with BSH 2020 and with the site's own normocytic-anaemia and microcytosis pages, which escalate only severe, symptomatic, late or unresponsive anaemia.

subject: magnesium
correct: MHRA (2012): hypomagnesaemia reported after at least 3 months of PPI use, and in most cases after about 1 year

fixes.new: duration (reported after as little as 3 months, most cases after about 1 year — MHRA)

note: The current wording suggests there is no risk before 1 year. The MHRA says cases occur from 3 months.

subject: magnesium

note: A per-cup figure is labelled as per 100 g. This is low risk; fix it for accuracy.
